policy: The route stylesheets were split out of wingman-route-overrides.css, which moved each page's rules into a file that loads after the shared remainder. This file is the reviewed answer for that move: one entry per page, saying why the page's own rules may load after the rules the shared file still holds for it, and pinning every pair whose order the split decides beneath that entry. A page with no entry, a pair that is not pinned as often as it occurs, a pinned pair that stopped occurring, and a page whose stylesheet no longer exists all fail the gate; the file only ratchets down. A pair is identified by its property, its importance, the specificity both rules share, the conditions they live under, and both selectors — never by a line number and never by a declared value — so editing a value does not unpin it, while a rule that moves out from under a width does. The check reads each page's own route scope on both sides, which is the population the split re-decided; a page rule against a shared rule no route scopes is a different question with a different owner and is not counted here.

pages.reason: Nothing is re-decided here: the call-coach rules the split moved load after the shared remainder's call-coach rules without tying with any of them, so the move cannot change a winner on that page.

The compare page's own layout rules load after the shared remainder's compare layout rules, and every tie below is a `display`, `gap`, `grid-template-columns`, `padding` or `text-align` decision between two separate regions of the page — the export menu, the steppers, the chip and filter strips, the page host — so the page stylesheet's copy is the later word on its own region rather than a shared rule being overruled.

The dashboard's own layout rules load after the shared remainder's dashboard rules, and every tie below is a `display`, `flex`, `gap`, `grid-template-columns`, `padding`, `width` or margin decision between the sidebar, the workspace, the app main column and the page host, so the page stylesheet's copy is the later word on the dashboard's own frame.
Nothing is re-decided here: the discovery rules the split moved load after the shared remainder's discovery rules without tying with any of them, so the move cannot change a winner on that page.

The glossary's own toolbar and term-list rules load after the shared remainder's glossary rules, and the ties below are `background`, `border-color` and `color` decisions between the toolbar's pressed buttons and the term list's active buttons. The two groups sit in separate sections of the page — the toolbar is a sibling of the workspace that holds the term list — so no element is inside both containers and no order between the two files can change a value either group renders. They are pinned rather than dropped because the pairing is invisible to a static reading, and a later edit that nests one group inside the other would make every one of these pairs live at once.

The projects page's own rules load after the shared remainder's projects rules, and the ties below are heading and section decisions between the project summary, the detail stack, the page host and the projects page wrapper. Read against the running page, one of them is live: the summary h2's `line-height`, where the page file's `1` beats the shared `1.15` and the heading renders at 26.4px rather than 30.36px at 885px wide, which is the tight leading that rule was written for. Its `font-size` twin cannot show, because the same file's `.wm-project-detail-stack > section:first-of-type h2` sets that property at a higher specificity and wins whatever the files' order. The section pairs cannot meet either: a section would have to be a direct child of both the detail stack and the page host. The `.wm-projects-page` and `[data-wingman-page="projects"]` wrappers do not contain the detail page at all, so those two heading pairs are impossible on that route.

Nothing is re-decided here: the sales-helper rules the split moved load after the shared remainder's sales-helper rules without tying with any of them, so the move cannot change a winner on that page.
Nothing is re-decided here: the settings rules the split moved load after the shared remainder that still carries the settings route scope, without tying with any of them.
